title: Runtime feature tagging and safe pin rollback policy for community model intake
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Clarify the metadata contract and operational rules for ingesting community/open model weights into the catalog when they expose runtime feature flags (e.g., rotary embeddings, KV cache layout variants, custom attention kernels). Define how runtime feature tags are recorded, surfaced in the Console and API, and how we perform safe pinning and automated rollback/unpin flows when regressions or incompatibilities are detected.
background: Recent onboarding attempts surfaced models with non-obvious runtime requirements (modified KV layout, custom attention hooks). These led to degraded latency or incorrect outputs when served using the default runtime profile.
Existing intake captures a free-form 'compatibility_notes' field but lacks structured flags that the runtime and routing layers can act on automatically.
PMs and runtime engineers need a deterministic contract so pinning decisions and fallbacks are safe and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Define a finite set of runtime feature tags and schema (string enum) that cover current incompatibility classes: kv_cache_layout_v1, kv_cache_layout_v2, rotary_embeddings, alibi_support, custom_attn_kernel, quant_layout_non_standard.
Catalog ingestion pipeline extracts and validates tags from model manifests and rejects manifests with unknown required tags unless an explicit opt-in flag is set.
Console shows feature tags on the model catalog entry and exposes a 'compatibility summary' badge and a link to the detailed runtime guidance doc.
Runtime routing uses tags to select compatible variants automatically; e.g., requests routed to a variant with matching kv_cache_layout or to a fallback instance if no match exists.

Pin policy: default soft-pin duration 14 days for community models, with an automatic telemetry-based health check (latency, error rate, quality regression) that can auto-unpin or mark the model as 'quarantined' after sustained regressions.
Rollback / unpin action is recorded in audit logs with actor, reason, metric evidence, and a reference to the failing eval set; Console allows owners to override with justification.
Unit and integration tests cover: manifest parsing for tags, routing selection logic, Console display, and the auto-unpin path triggered by a simulated degradation window.
Migration plan for existing catalog entries: 90% of entries have tags inferred heuristically and surfaced as 'inferred (needs review)'.
decisions: Use an explicit enum for tags instead of free-form text to make routing deterministic and enable fast rejection of unsupported manifests.
Implement 'soft-pin' by default for community models to reduce long-lived mis-pins; enterprise-owned models remain hard-pinnable via an admin flag.
Telemetry-driven unpin thresholds will be conservative initially (e.g., 2x baseline error rate sustained for 60 minutes) and tuned based on canary results.
Present inferred tags with a 'review required' CTA in Console for models where we guessed tags from heuristics (e.g., tokenizer checks, model config markers).
tradeoffs: Strict enum tags improve safety but require ongoing maintenance as new model architectures appear; adds short-term friction for model contributors.
Automatic unpin reduces customer exposure to regressions but risks false positives; mitigated by conservative thresholds and a manual override path.
Adding tag enforcement in ingestion increases rejection rate during rollout; we'll use a phased gate (warning -> opt-in -> block) to reduce churn.
Inferred tags accelerate migration but create a trust gap; requiring human review for inferred tags adds operational overhead.
notes_and_links: Telemetry dashboard for candidate unpin heuristics: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/CatalogUnpin/overview
